audits.title: Using clinical indicators in a quality improvement programme targeting cardiac care.
audits.standard: Expert-panel clinical indicators of evidence-based care for acute coronary syndromes and congestive heart failure (40 process indicators)
audits.setting: Brisbane Cardiac Consortium: three hospitals and five divisions of general practice

cycle1.result: Indicators reliable (kappa 0.7-1.0); on independent review of indicator-failed in-hospital cases, clinically legitimate reasons for withholding interventions were found for 27 of 28 process indicators.

audits.intervention: Indicators fed back every 6 months (hospitals) and 10 months (general practice) with an education programme and customised analyses on request.

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in 17 of 40 process indicators over the course of the project.

audits.other_findings: Lessons included keeping feedback brief, limiting data items and using cheaper data collection such as scannable forms.
audits.citation: Hickey A, Scott I, Denaro C, Stewart N, Bennett C, Theile T. Using clinical indicators in a quality improvement programme targeting cardiac care. Int J Qual Health Care. 2004;16 Suppl 1:i11-25. doi:10.1093/intqhc/mzh032. PMID: 15059983.

audits.title: Management of patients admitted with an Acute Coronary Syndrome in New Zealand: results of a comprehensive nationwide audit.
audits.standard: Evidence-based investigations, revascularisation and discharge medications for acute coronary syndrome

cycle1.result: Echocardiogram 20%, exercise test 20%, angiogram 21%; discharge aspirin 82%, clopidogrel 8%, beta-blockers 63%, ACE inhibitors 43%, statins 55% (n=695).

audits.other_findings: PCI rates 13%, 8% and 4% for STEMI, non-STEMI and unstable angina; CABG 4%, 3% and 4%.
audits.citation: Ellis C, Gamble G, French J, Devlin G, Matsis P, Elliott J, et al.. Management of patients admitted with an Acute Coronary Syndrome in New Zealand: results of a comprehensive nationwide audit. N Z Med J. 2004;117(1197):U953. PMID: 15326506.

audits.title: Current management of acute coronary syndromes in Australia: observations from the acute coronary syndromes prospective audit.
audits.standard: Guideline evidence-based therapies and invasive management for ACS
audits.setting: 39 metropolitan, regional and rural sites (ACS Prospective Audit registry)

cycle1.result: Angiography use: STEMI 89%, high-risk NSTEACS 54%, intermediate-risk NSTEACS 34%; an evidence-practice gap was described.

audits.other_findings: Evidence-practice gap was not matched by higher in-hospital event risk.
audits.citation: Chew DP, Amerena J, Coverdale S, Rankin J, Astley C, Brieger D. Current management of acute coronary syndromes in Australia: observations from the acute coronary syndromes prospective audit. Intern Med J. 2007;37(11):741-748. doi:10.1111/j.1445-5994.2007.01435.x. PMID: 17645500.

audits.title: Patients admitted with an acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in New Zealand in 2007: results of a second comprehensive nationwide audit and a comparison with the first audit from 2002.
audits.standard: Guideline recommended risk stratification after ACS

cycle1.result: Risk stratification by treadmill test or angiogram in 48%; exercise tests 21%, echocardiograms 19%, angiography 32%; PCI 19%, CABG 2.8%.

audits.other_findings: Compared with the 2002 audit (n=930): exercise tests 20%, echocardiograms 20%, angiography 21%; care had not substantially changed in 5 years.
audits.citation: Ellis C, Gamble G, Hamer A, Williams M, Matsis P, Elliott J, et al.. Patients admitted with an acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in New Zealand in 2007: results of a second comprehensive nationwide audit and a comparison with the first audit from 2002. audits.title: The management of acute coronary syndrome patients across New Zealand in 2012: results of a third comprehensive nationwide audit and observations of current interventional care.
audits.setting: 39 hospitals across New Zealand (NZ ACS Audit / ANZ SNAPSHOT)

cycle1.result: Echocardiogram 29%, exercise test 23%, CT angiogram 4%, coronary angiogram 33%; non-intervention centre patients less likely to have echocardiography (25 vs 31%) and had significant delays to invasive assessment.

audits.other_findings: Third nationwide audit; STEMI 10%, NSTEMI 26%, unstable angina 17%.
audits.citation: Ellis C, Gamble G, Devlin G, Elliott J, Hamer A, Williams M, et al.. The management of acute coronary syndrome patients across New Zealand in 2012: results of a third comprehensive nationwide audit and observations of current interventional care. N Z Med J. 2013;126(1387):36-68. PMID: 24362734.

audits.title: Time to treatment in patients of suspected acute coronary syndrome in Pakistan: a clinical audit.
audits.standard: ACC/AHA guideline benchmarks: physician review, ECG, aspirin and anticoagulant within 10 min; primary PCI within 90 min
audits.setting: Emergency department, tertiary care facility (Aga Khan University), Karachi

cycle1.result: 74.1% seen by physician within 10 min of triage; ECG within 10 min in 93 (47.7%); aspirin within 10 min in 41.9% of 207; anticoagulants within 10 min in 32.9% of 155; half of primary PCI patients within 90 min.

audits.citation: Khursheed M, Fayyaz J, Feroze A, Shakeel N, Bhatti JA. Time to treatment in patients of suspected acute coronary syndrome in Pakistan: a clinical audit. Heart Lung. 2015;44(1):63-67. doi:10.1016/j.hrtlng.2014.08.007. PMID: 25281530.

audits.title: Management of non ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome patients in New Zealand: a longitudinal analysis. Results from the New Zealand Acute Coronary Syndrome national audits of 2002, 2007 and 2012.
audits.setting: Hospitals in New Zealand, national ACS audits

cycle1.result: Important limitations to NSTEACS care demonstrated (no figures given in abstract).

audits.intervention: National audit and feedback creating momentum for change (repeated audits).

cycle2.result: More patients had echocardiography and coronary angiography; evidence-based in-hospital medical treatment and revascularisation increased (no figures given).

audits.other_findings: An intermediate audit was done in 2007; considerable room remains to improve prompt referral for angiography.
audits.citation: Devlin G, Williams M, Elliott J, White HD, French J, Gamble G, et al.. Management of non ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome patients in New Zealand: a longitudinal analysis. Results from the New Zealand Acute Coronary Syndrome national audits of 2002, 2007 and 2012. N Z Med J. 2016;129(1428):10-16. PMID: 26914189.

audits.title: Low-dose intensive insulin therapy in patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome accompanied by Left Ventricular Failure: audit of two UK hospitals.
audits.standard: Normoglycaemia (4-8 mmol/l) for a consecutive six-hour period with a low-dose insulin regimen
audits.setting: Two UK hospitals (North Bristol NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: Normoglycaemia for six consecutive hours achieved in 72% of patients within a median of 13 hours.

audits.intervention: New low-dose intravenous insulin regimen for ACS with left ventricular failure, introduced after local audit showed more hypoglycaemia in this group.
audits.other_findings: The audit reported here measured practice after the new regimen; earlier local audit data are not given numerically.
audits.citation: Manning N, Albarran JW. Low-dose intensive insulin therapy in patients with Acute Coronary Syndrome accompanied by Left Ventricular Failure: audit of two UK hospitals. J Clin Nurs. 2016;25(19-20):3001-3009. doi:10.1111/jocn.13257. PMID: 27118423.

audits.title: Knowledge translation lessons from an audit of Aboriginal Australians with acute coronary syndrome presenting to a regional hospital.
audits.setting: Regional Western Australian hospital emergency department

cycle1.result: Emergency department management of Aboriginal and non-Aboriginal acute coronary syndrome patients compared (figures not given).

audits.intervention: Reporting of audit findings and advocacy tailored to institutional hierarchy and audiences.

cycle2.result: Follow-up audit showed general improvement in guideline adherence and reduced treatment inequalities for Aboriginal patients (figures not given).

audits.other_findings: The paper is mainly an interview-based case study of knowledge translation.

audits.title: Management of suspected acute coronary syndrome patients admitted to cardiology or non-cardiology services at Auckland City Hospital: implications for future national data collection.
audits.setting: Auckland City Hospital, cardiology and non-cardiology services

cycle1.result: 45 (37%) managed by cardiology and 76 (63%) by non-cardiology services; definite ACS 27/45 (60%) vs 16/76 (21%). Non-cardiology patients with definite ACS were less likely to receive guideline-recommended care.

audits.other_findings: About one-third of ACS patients were managed by non-cardiology services and would not be captured by ANZACS-QI.
audits.citation: Wang TKM, Chow KL, Lin A, Chataline A, White H, Dawes M, et al.. Management of suspected acute coronary syndrome patients admitted to cardiology or non-cardiology services at Auckland City Hospital: implications for future national data collection. N Z Med J. 2018;131(1471):30-39. PMID: 29518797.

audits.title: Dropping risk stratification with subsequent treatment-risk paradox in non ST elevation acute coronary syndromes: a clinical audit in Iraq.
audits.standard: Guideline-recommended risk stratification with TIMI and GRACE scores to guide invasive strategy
audits.setting: Multicentre prospective study including Baghdad Heart Centre

cycle1.result: TIMI score calculated in 5.3% and GRACE in none; invasive strategy in 85.24% and 82.7% of low GRACE and TIMI risk vs 42.85% and 40% of high-risk patients.

audits.other_findings: Most patients with acute heart failure (60%), ongoing chest pain (80.76%), dynamic ST changes (85%) and cardiogenic shock (80%) were managed conservatively.
audits.citation: Dakhil ZA, Farhan HA. Dropping risk stratification with subsequent treatment-risk paradox in non ST elevation acute coronary syndromes: a clinical audit in Iraq. BMC Health Serv Res. 2021;21(1):1015. doi:10.1186/s12913-021-07034-7. PMID: 34565377.
